header.title: De Regibus Apostaticis: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Lucifer, Bishop of Cagliari
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's stoa0180a.stoa003.opp-lat1, from Open Greek and Latin's CSEL (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. The whole work is translated. It was chosen because no English translation of it could be found.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation of the whole work, checked against the original by a second AI only in samples. No specialist has reviewed it.
header.availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's CSEL and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

notes.urn:cts:latinLit:stoa0180a.stoa003.opp-l: Lucifer calls Gideon 'Ierobabel son of Iosias'; rendered Jerubbaal son of Joash, as in Judges. 'Epkrath' read as Ephrath (Ophrah in Judges). The biblical quotations follow an Old Latin text that differs from the Vulgate in places, e.g. 'non relinquebant ad uitam huic Israel' and 'dux sceptrorum'; these are translated as given. In 'quoniam audiui in filiis Iesse' the sense seems to require 'I have seen' (uidi), and I have translated it so. The phrase 'quid sentis arbitrari nos posse Christianos eripi' is awkward; it is rendered by its likely sense.

The biblical quotations follow an Old Latin text close to the Septuagint, with garbled names; I have kept them as given: Ader the Idumaean (Hadad the Edomite), Esrom son of Anadeth (Rezon son of Eliada), Bemathad and Adragas king of Saba (Hadadezer king of Zobah), Sariram (Zeruah), Cama (Chemosh), Achiab (Ahijah), Anna (Ano in the Septuagint), Baria and Arira (Sarira). 'Damasic' is taken as Damascus. 'Satan' is kept as in the text, meaning 'adversary'. Scanning errors corrected: 'in semis' read as 'in servis', 'ei istius' as 'ex istius', 'nonum' as 'novum', 'Bethd' as 'Bethel', and stray marks ('tantum\'', 's o') dropped. In 3.1, 'nouo periturus exemplo' and 'non nouum' are taken as 'unheard-of'. Pancratius is presumably Lucifer's fellow envoy, the Roman presbyter Pancratius. 'Hilarius' is probably the deacon Hilary, not Hilary of Poitiers.

Line 6.1: 'um eius fiMi regnaremus' is garbled; read as 'numquam eius filii regnaremus'. 'Basiam filium Achiae' is Baasha son of Ahijah; 'Iambre' is Omri (LXX Ambri); 'filius Asab' is Jehoshaphat son of Asa; 'Hela' (for Ethbaal) appears corrupt, and 'Basan et' looks intrusive; 'quia ita exempti sint, inpune ... cedere' is awkward and translated as 'go unpunished'. Evident scanning errors read silently: 'aides' = uides, 'nisus' = uisus, 'quii' = qui. Line 7.1: 'filius Ader' = Ben-hadad; 'uieit' = uicit; 'post tanta funera tua' taken as 'after so many killings of yours'.

The 'Jeroboam son of Joash' is Jeroboam II. 'The son of Amaziah' and 'Uzziah' are the same king (also called Azariah). Lucifer gives Manasseh's son as 'Amos'; this is Amon. Scanning errors corrected silently: 'Escchias' (Hezekiah), 'dexid' (David), 'Israd' (Israel), 'acternum' (aeternum). In the quotation from Kings the phrase 'quam elegi et omnibus tribubus' is read as 'ex omnibus tribubus', 'out of all the tribes'. 'Ad hoc te fingis Christianum' is taken as purposive: 'you pretend to be a Christian for this purpose'.

Several scanning errors read as evident: paccator = peccator, mal ilia = malitia, portibus = partibus, nota ignorans = non ignorans, aem$n> = semen, aat = aut, d = et. 'Certis non statim reddi' is unclear (perhaps 'meritis' or 'cito'); rendered as 'their deserts not at once repaid'. 'å ita est' read as 'si ita est'. Stray 'm' before 'eo usque' omitted. 'Ut dicas... faciunt illi' taken as 'that you say this is the work of those who...'. In the Psalm citation the text has 'iudicia eius'; rendered 'your judgements'—better 'his judgements', consistent with the Latin.

'ut paenitearis' stands loosely after 'patientem esse'; taken as purpose ('so that you may repent'). 'dig.. nati' read as 'dignati'; '(in) se habent' supplied by the edition, rendered 'what they have [in their hearts]'. 'indulgentiam funerum tuorum' is unusual; 'funera' taken as 'killings' (cf. 'homicida' earlier), though 'deaths' (i.e. pardon from your [spiritual] deaths) is possible. Joel's 'malitiam inrogatam' (the evil threatened/imposed) is rendered literally.

nodes.text: Since you are pleased to keep using the saying that if you did not both believe soundly and if the things you do to us were not pleasing to God, you would already have been destroyed, I have wished to lay open to you the deeds of a few kings who were your equals in apostasy and cruelty, so that that voice of yours may be buried, which says: 'If the faith of Arius, that is, my faith, were not catholic, if it were not pleasing to God that I persecute that faith which they wrote against us at Nicaea, I would certainly never still be flourishing in power.' I make no mention of those kings who were strangers to the knowledge of God; I deal only with those who are known to have reigned in Judaea. In the book of Judges we find that Jerubbaal son of Joash was chosen by God, and it was said to him: 'Go in your strength, and you will save Israel from the hand of Midian. See, do I not send you?' And below: 'I will be with you, and you will strike Midian as one man.' This Midian, scripture says, had a multitude like the sand of the sea. But when everything that God had promised Gideon had been fulfilled, when he saw himself raised up from lowliness, enriched from poverty, made king from the condition of a commoner, what does he immediately do? He says, of course, to the people: 'Give me, each of you, an earring from his spoil.' And when he had received a weight of golden earrings of up to one thousand seven hundred shekels, besides the bracelets and necklaces and coverings and purple which were on the kings of Midian, and besides the golden collars which [were] on the necks of the enemies' camels, what does sacred scripture say Gideon did? 'And Gideon made them into an ephod, and set it up in his city Ophrah; and the sons of Israel committed fornication there, and it became a stumbling-block to Gideon and to his house.' Did he put it off for some days, and only then work this wicked work against God? Was he able to remember, when he had set about doing these things, that God had said to him: 'Go, I will be with you'? Where is that [deed], that according to God's command he demolished Baal and cut down his groves and offered sacrifice to God? Where is that which he said to the messenger of God when he said to him: 'The Lord is with you, mighty in strength'? 'On me, Lord; and if the Lord is with us, why then have all these evils seized us? And where are his wonders, which our fathers related to us, saying: Did not God bring us out of Egypt? And now the Lord has spurned us and handed us over into the hand of Midian.' Did he recall, at the time when he undertook to act against God, that those evils had befallen them because of idolatry? But when they had been rescued, so as to live without fear of their enemies, from all those evils with which he said he and the whole people had been weighed down, at once he does a thing through which both he himself and the whole people alike would be handed over into the hands of their enemies because of idolatry. He had heard from God that because they had served idols, having forsaken God, all those evils had befallen them; he remembered that the prophet had spoken, and yet on the very day on which their enemies had become nothing before them, that king, whom you are pleased to resemble, judged in his folly that idols should be served rather than God, who had granted him those things. 'And the sons of Israel', says scripture, 'did evil before the Lord God, and he handed [them] over into the hands of Midian for seven years, and the hand of Midian prevailed greatly over Israel. And Israel made for themselves, before the face of Midian, hiding-places in the mountains, and caves and tombs. And it happened that when Israel sowed, Midian and Amalek and the sons of the East came up, and they came up against him and engaged with them and ruined the territory of the land, as far as you come to Gaza, and they left for this Israel no means of life, no sheep nor calf nor ass. For they and their beasts came up, and they brought their tents and led their camels, and came like locusts in multitude, for there was no number, and they came upon the land to ruin it. And Israel was made poor before the face of Midian. And the sons of Israel cried to the Lord, and it happened, because the sons of Israel had cried to the Lord on account of Midian, the Lord sent a man, a prophet, to the sons of Israel, and he said to them: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: I am he who brought you out of Egypt and led you out of the house of slavery, and took you from the hand of the king of Egypt and from the hand of all who persecuted you, and I cast them out before your face and gave you their land. And I said to you: I am the Lord your God; you shall not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; and you did not listen to my voice.' What does Jerubbaal, who is also called Gideon, do after this rebuke of the Lord? As soon as he sees his enemy brought to nothing, as soon as all those adversaries, who are said to have been like the sand of the sea, were slaughtered, and not by a huge number of Israelites but by three hundred men, as soon as he saw all the foreign kings killed, he contrives that thing through which the sons of Israel could sin against God; and yet he is found to have reigned here in Israel forty years even after so great a crime had been committed. It will not, then, be a wonder if you too, sacrilegious as you are, still live on in the body, since you see that King Gideon lived forty years after committing idolatry, and kept possession of his kingdom; for sacred scripture says that the Israelites had rest for forty years, and that enemies were not permitted against them at all, nor did any of the foreigners have dominion over them, because they had cried out to God. Such benefits did God confer on your fellow-sacrilegists, showing himself indeed to be all-powerful, but them unworthy to obtain rest, since not even for one day after receiving rest from such great dangers did they choose to serve him who had shown such great mercy. Though the Israelites were such, yet in his goodness he spared them even when after this they practised idolatry, and he did not repay at once, but later, at the time that pleased him, he did repay; the guilt of idolatry could not pass from them unpunished. So too, Constantius, he will pay you back, unless you look to yourself in the meantime. If the Israelites, serving demons and forsaking God, when they had already become strangers to the knowledge of God, were nevertheless heard and freed from the hand of Midian and from all their persecutors as soon as it entered their hearts that he is the all-powerful God who had led their fathers out of the land of Egypt, what do you think we must suppose about whether we Christians can be rescued from your hands? Or do you deny, or, as far as I know, do you not clearly see, that we worship only the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and of all the prophets, apostles and martyrs? Believe me, we have been heard and we will be heard, so that you, with all your fragile loftiness, may lie beneath the heel of all his servants; but that there are some brief delays, so that he does not yet, by destroying you Arians, grant his holy church the full security of peace, the reason is this: that it is fitting, while you rage as our adversary, that all should come to be proved.

You say: 'If I had done wrong, if I held heresy, God would already have taken vengeance on me.' You hear sacred scripture saying that the Lord spared even a foreign people for a long time, and yet afterwards they received the deserts of their deeds. Samuel said to Saul: 'The Lord sent me to anoint you as king over Israel, and now hear the voice of the word of the Lord: Thus says the Lord almighty: Now I will avenge what Amalek did to you, Israel, how he opposed you on the way by which you went up from Egypt. And now go and you shall strike Amalek and all that is his, and you shall not covet anything of theirs, but you shall exterminate him and put him under the ban, him and all that is his, and you shall not spare him, and you shall kill all that is his, from man to woman and from infant to nursing mother.' And below: 'And Saul came to the city of Amalek, and approached and besieged Amalek in the ravine. And Saul said to the Kenite: Go, turn aside from the midst, and turn aside from Amalek, and do not join yourself with him, since you showed mercy to the sons of Israel when they went up out of Egypt. And the Kenite turned aside from the midst of Amalek, and Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, which is opposite Egypt. And Saul took Agag king of Amalek alive, and killed all his people with the edge of the sword.' You see how, though late, they received [the penalty for] the deed of their crime, and you say: 'Unless I were acting rightly, I would never reign long.' We find that Saul himself also, because he acted against the Lord's command, was rejected, and yet reigned long after his rejection, after God said to Samuel: 'I repent that I anointed Saul as king.' And you say: 'Unless I had believed rightly, unless I lived as is pleasing to God, I would certainly never be ruling until now.' And so that you may fully take in what we say concerning Saul, hear what he did against the Lord's command: 'And Saul and all his people took Agag the king, and the best of the flocks and herds and of the food and the vineyards and of all good things, and they would not destroy all the good things, but they kept back every precious work and destroyed the worthless. And the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying: I repent that I set up Saul as king, since he has turned away from me and has not established my words. And Samuel was grieved and cried to God all night and before dawn, and Samuel went to meet Israel.' And below: 'And Samuel came to Saul, and behold, Saul was offering a whole burnt offering to the Lord, and the first of the spoils which he brought from Amalek. And Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him: Blessed are you to the Lord; I have established all that the Lord spoke. And Samuel said: And what is this voice of the flock in my ears, and the voice of the oxen which I hear? And Saul said: I brought from Amalek what the people took as spoil, the best of the flock and of the oxen, so that they may be sacrificed to the Lord your God, the king; but the rest I destroyed and exterminated. And Samuel said to Saul: Were you not the least in [your own] sight, a leader of the sceptres from the tribe of Israel, and the Lord anointed you king over Israel, and the Lord sent you on the way and said to you: Go and destroy those who sin against me, Amalek, and you shall fight them until you consume them? And why did you not hear the voice of the Lord, but rushed upon the spoil and did what is evil before the Lord? And Saul said: Because I listened to the people; I went on the way on which God sent me, and brought Agag king of Amalek, and destroyed Amalek. And the people took spoil of the flock and the choicest herds of those whom I destroyed, to sacrifice before the Lord our God in Gilgal. And Samuel said: Does the Lord want whole burnt offerings and sacrifices more than hearing the voice of the Lord? And behold, obedience to what is said is better than sacrifice, and obedience than the fat of rams. Since sin is an abomination, you have brought pains and groans upon yourself. Because you made the word of the Lord of no account, the Lord will make you of no account, so that you do not reign. And Saul said to Samuel: I have sinned, since I passed over the word of the Lord and your word, because I feared the people and listened to their voice. And now take away my sin, return with me, I will worship the Lord your God. And Samuel said to him: The Lord will tear your kingdom from Israel out of your hand today, and will give it to your neighbour, who is better than you.' And below: 'And Samuel did not again see Saul until the day of his death, since Samuel mourned for Saul, and the Lord repented that he had made Saul king over Israel. And the Lord said to Samuel: How long will you mourn for Saul? Behold, I am driving him out so that he does not reign over Israel; fill your horn with oil and come, I will send you to Jesse in Bethlehem, since I have seen among the sons of Jesse [one] as king for me.' Now you will be able to recognise, Constantius, that even those rejected by the Lord, even those destined for eternal death, reign long after committing a grave offence, since you see that after David, the glorious son of Jesse, had been anointed king, Saul nevertheless reigned long and even had power to persecute him whom God had chosen for himself as prophet and king: the wicked man persecuted the good, the unjust the just, the one hateful to God the one whom God loved. Since this is so, do not boast that after perpetrating so great a crime you are still living, as Saul lived; but consider what kind of punishment came upon Saul, which can also come upon you unless you take thought for yourself. For if the Lord was so angered against him, first because he took spoil against the prohibition, second because he persecuted David, his man, how much more must the punishment of his anger come upon you, upon you whose crimes are so enormous that you have even come into the guilt of sacrilege.

'If I had acted wrongly,' you say, 'if I were a heretic, as Lucifer says, God would already have taken the kingdom from me.' Learn, then, that Solomon too lived on after committing idolatry, and be so good as to understand that you too are such as he was after his idolatry. 'And the Lord raised up a satan against Solomon, Ader the Idumaean, and Esrom son of Anadeth in Bemathad, Adragas king of Saba his lord. And men gathered against him, and he was leader of the band, and he seized the city of Damascus and settled in it and reigned in Damascus, and they were satans to Solomon and to Israel all the days of Solomon.' We have proved to you that Solomon also reigned for some years after his idolatry, serving by then not God but the devil, which is why he is marked out as having clung to diabolical men. So you too cling to your fellow-sacrilegists the Arians, and although you are still in the body, although you remain on the throne, you are nevertheless found to be such as Solomon was after he forsook God and followed idols. You wanted us to cling to such men as Solomon made the Israelites cling to. Where was that love of God which the holy scriptures relate was in Solomon, at the time when he saw fit to follow idols and forsake God? Where did this come from, unless that he had become a man wholly estranged from sober understanding? I do not want you to applaud yourself that, though you are a blasphemer and a destroyer of the religion of God, you still hold the kingdom and are proud after your sacrilege, since we find that Rehoboam too, the son of Solomon, practised idolatry and lived on the throne for twenty years. For holy scripture says of him: 'And king Solomon slept with his fathers in the city of David; and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place in Jerusalem, and he was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty years in Jerusalem.' And below: 'And he did evil in the sight of the Lord and did not walk in the way of David his father.' Since, then, both Solomon, from the time he saw fit to give himself over to idols, and his son Rehoboam, who was always serving idols, though they did not walk in the paths of David, nevertheless lived on the throne and both reached the last day of their lives reigning, why do you wonder to yourself that, though you live on in that crime after committing the sacrilege, you are proud as king, because neither kingdom nor life is taken from you by God? For you see that Jeroboam too tried, as you do, to overturn the religion of the Lord from its foundations, and yet he lived on for a great many years, and indeed remained in that crime, as it is written: 'And there was a man from mount Ephraim, a servant of Solomon, and his name was Jeroboam, and his mother's name was Sariram, a harlot'; and in another place: 'And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned from Egypt, they sent and called him into the assembly and made him king in Israel'; and below: 'And Jeroboam said in his heart: Now the kingdom will return to David. If this people goes up to offer sacrifice in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, the heart of the people will also turn to their lord Rehoboam, king of Judah. Then Jeroboam took thought and went, and made two golden heifers and said to the people: Let it suffice you to have gone up to Jerusalem. Behold your gods, Israel, who brought you back from the land of Egypt. And he set one in Bethel and put one in Dan. And this thing became a sin, and the people went before the face of the one heifer as far as Dan. And they made houses on the high places, and he made priests from some part of the people, who were not of the sons of Levi. And Jeroboam made a feast day in the eighth month, on the fifteenth of the month, like the feast day of Judah, and he went up to the sanctuary which he had made in Bethel, to sacrifice before the heifers which he had made, and he appointed in Bethel priests of the high places which he had made. And he went up to the sanctuary which he had made on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, on the feast day which he had devised out of his own heart, and he made a feast day for the sons of Israel.'

So do not boast that, though you practise idolatry, you still live in possession of the glory of the kingdom, since you see that this Jeroboam made golden heifers and turned the people of the Israelites to idolatry, and yet was not only not destroyed as soon as he had sinned, but was even permitted to live long. Could God not have removed those idolatrous kings? But it has been shown how ungrateful you are to God, you who, though you are so greatly exalted, not only forget him who exalts you but even go on persecuting him in his servants, desiring to remove his religion from the midst. Learn that this is so from the deed of that king Jeroboam: though he was the son of a slave-woman, though he remembered that he was born of a harlot, though he received the kingdom of his lord Solomon to the disgrace of that same Solomon, why did he forsake God and turn himself to idols? Although, I say, Jeroboam knew that the kingdom had been given him by God because Solomon his lord had followed idols, he nevertheless counted all this as nothing and resolved to make idols, and to be given over to them, with all the people who served God, rather than to the living God, who from the son of a harlot had made him hold the kingdom of Solomon his lord. Do not wonder, then, that he spares you ungrateful men who sin against him; but I urge you to see this, that, late though it may be, if you remain in this wickedness of yours, you will receive what all your predecessors in sacrilege received. We urge you to be so good as to rescue yourself from such great evils. And you have <examples> besides; you are not the first to do this. We see that this Jeroboam also counted the Lord's warning as nothing. 'And it came to pass,' it says, 'at that time, that Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, and Ahijah the Shilonite, the prophet, found him on the road, and Ahijah was covered with a new garment, and the two of them were in the field. And Ahijah took hold of his new garment which he had on him and tore it into twelve pieces and said to Jeroboam: Take ten pieces for yourself, for thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give you ten sceptres; and two sceptres shall be his for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of the city of Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel; because Solomon has forsaken me and has made [offerings] to Astarte, the unclean idol of the Sidonians, and to Cama, the idol of Moab, and to their king, the religion of the sons of Ammon, and he has not walked in my ways, to do what is right before me, as David his father did. And I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand in the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant whom I chose, since I will act against him all the days of his life. And I will take the kingdom from the hand of his son and will give you ten sceptres, but to his son I will give two sceptres, so that there may be a place for my servant David all his days before me in the city of Jerusalem, which I have chosen for myself to put my name there. And I will take you, and you shall reign over whatever your soul desires, and you shall be king in Israel. And it shall be, if you keep all that I command you and walk in my ways and do what is right in my sight and keep my precepts and my commandments as David my servant did, then I will be with you and will build you a faithful house, as I built for David.' When a man born of a harlot, a man who remembered that he was born of servile stock, heard these things from God, did he, after everything the Lord had promised was fulfilled, comply with him who had promised him so much? Did he not, as soon as he saw himself exalted, set out against him? Did not Jeroboam at once take pains that God should be forsaken by all his worshippers?

You are told by us that unless you correct yourself, unless you begin to walk in ways pleasing to God, you will perish after an unheard-of example; and you remain in your iniquity, you persevere in your sacrilege. It is not unheard-of, since to this king Jeroboam God had the things already mentioned conveyed through his man, and, when his son was held by a grave illness, he sent to God's servant and heard what was to come; and yet, when he saw even the evils foretold to him being fulfilled, he acted more and more against God and wanted God's house destroyed. 'And there was a man,' it says, 'from Shiloh, and his name was Achiab, and he was sixty years old, and the word of the Lord was with him. And Jeroboam said to his wife: Rise and take in your hand loaves for the man of God, and cakes for his children, and grapes and a jar of honey. And the woman rose and did as her husband told her. And Achiab was a very old man, and his eyes were dim so that he could not see. And the woman rose from Baria and went. And it came to pass, when she had entered the city to Achiab the Shilonite, Achiab said to his servant: Go out now to meet Anna, the wife of Jeroboam, and say to her: Come in and do not stand, for thus says the Lord: I am sending harsh things upon you. And Anna went in to the man of God, and Achiab said to her: Why have you brought me loaves and grapes and cakes and a jar of honey? Thus says the Lord: Behold, you will go from me, and it shall be, when you enter the gate of the city of Arira, your girls will come out to meet you and will say to you: The boy is dead. For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will destroy from this Jeroboam [everyone] who pisses against the wall; and Jeroboam's dead shall be in the city, and the dogs shall eat them, and his dead shall be in the field, and the birds of the sky shall eat them.' It is not, I say, unheard-of if you persist in this obstinacy, since you know that this Jeroboam was not deterred by all these things. For at once, as the man of God had said, as the woman entered the city their son died; and yet Jeroboam did not perceive what God would pay him back with because he had forsaken him and had made the people perish with him, nor did he fear, from his son's death, that the rest might follow him too, but he grew old in his cunning. So far, indeed, had Jeroboam become out of his mind, from the time he withdrew from him who had given him the kingdom, that after he had said, 'Go to the man of God and learn whether our son is to die,' and had learned through the man of God that not only was their son to die but dangers also threatened his whole kingdom, he nevertheless, as he had once resolved, preferred to serve the devil. He sends to the man of God to inquire about the future, and him to whose man he sends he spurns, and to insult his majesty he makes heifers and makes the people worship them with him. He did these things, and yet he was not destroyed on the spot, but survived long on the throne. And you say: 'If I had been a heretic, if, as Lucifer, Pancratius and Hilary say, I were attacking the religion of God, it would already have been avenged on me.' Learn further what befell this king Jeroboam, and yet how even so he was not turned to God, but rather died persevering in his crime and perished in his sacrilege: 'And Jeroboam made a feast day in the eighth month, on the feast day of the fifteenth of the month, like the feast day of Judah, and he went up to the sacrifice which he had made in Bethel, that they might sacrifice to the heifers which he had made, and he appointed in Bethel priests of the high places which he had made, and he went up to the sanctuary which he had made on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, on the feast day which he had devised out of his own heart, and he made a feast day for the sons of Israel and went up to the sanctuary to sacrifice. And behold, a man of God from Judah came by the word of the Lord to Bethel, and Jeroboam was standing at his altar to sacrifice; and the prophet called out against the altar by the word of the Lord, saying: O sanctuary, sanctuary, thus says the Lord: Behold, a son shall be born in the house of David, and Josiah shall be his name, and he shall sacrifice upon you the priests of the high places who sacrifice upon you, and he shall burn men's bones upon you. And on that day he will give the sign which the Lord has spoken: Behold, the sanctuary shall be split apart and the fat that is on it shall be poured out. And it came to pass, when he heard the words of the man of God calling out against the altar that was in Bethel, he stretched out his hand towards the altar, saying: Seize him. And the king's hand which he stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back to himself. And the sacrifice was split apart, and its fat was poured out from the sanctuary, according to the sign which the man of God had spoken by the word of the Lord. And the king answered and said to the man of God: Entreat the face of the Lord your God, that my hand may be restored to me. And the man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before.' When he had seen fulfilled both the signs uttered by the mouth of the man of God, and his impious arm, stretched out to kill the man of God, suddenly withered for terror and at once, through the prayer of God's worshipper, made whole again, did he do away with the idolatry he himself had set up? Did he at last remove from the midst the feast day which he had devised out of his own heart? Not at all; rather he is found to have met the day of his death in that obstinacy of his presumption. So we will not be able to wonder if (God avert it from you) you resolve to meet the day of your death in your heresy, since even by signs and wonders your fellow-sacrilegists before you could not be called back to worshipping God alone. For holy scripture says of Jeroboam: 'And after this Jeroboam did not turn back from his wickedness, but turned again and made priests of the high places from part of the people. Whoever wished raised his hand, and became a priest on the high places. And this thing became a sin to the house of Jeroboam, to its ruin and its extermination from the face of the earth.'

So that these things may not be said of you too, I beg you to rescue yourself from the abominable company of the Arians; I beg you to become a Christian, as you were before, instead of an Arian. And do not be angry with us for setting your acts beside Jeroboam's; rather, I implore you, see that I am pressing all these things on you for the good of your salvation, and that they should be called instructions rather than rebukes. For we compare you to Jeroboam because in our times you have tried to turn everyone away from God, just as he tried to make the people of Israel apostate from being worshippers of God. I do not want you to promise yourself any hope from this, that you do evil and yet reign, when you see that Jeroboam too reigned long in his crime, and also that the son of Solomon, likewise practising idolatry, died in the same crime; and likewise his son Abijam, of whom I find it written: 'And he went in the sins of his father, which he did before him, and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as the heart of David his father was.' And yet, though they served idols, they remained on the throne and died in that rank, and handed the authority of the kingdom on to their sons. So do not applaud yourself over this either, that your father handed the kingdom on to you, saying: 'Had my father not done well to join the Arians, we his sons would never reign.' I do not want you to say: 'If I were a heretic, I would never rule so greatly; God would never let me remain on the throne till now,' when you see that Baasha son of Ahijah reigned twenty-four years over Israel, of whom you have found it written in the third book of Kingdoms: 'And he did evil before the Lord and went in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, and in his sins, as he made Israel sin.' This king Baasha certainly ought to have feared being struck down like Jeroboam, if he had departed from the ways of the Lord. But you who turn aside from God are such that, once it has pleased you to take up the service of idolatry to God's injury, you cannot be frightened even by the example of those already judged and be converted to God. It is written also of king Omri: 'And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and did more evil than all who were before him, and went in all the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat in his sins.' And yet this man, who is said to have sinned more than all the kings who had been before him, was not wiped out as soon as he forsook God, nor was he afflicted by any grave illness, so that he who is described as having sinned more gravely might be seen to be destroyed by a graver punishment. You see, Constantius, that even if it falls to you to pass this temporal life in the highest good fortune, you ought all the more to fear that you are being reserved for the judgement of God. And although even those who are wiped out at once, on whom some punishment is inflicted here by God, are always tormented after their descent, yet if you are snatched away from here while living in the highest good fortune, consider how vengeance will proceed against you, who are found in so great a crime. So do not credit yourself with any good fortune on this account, that though you deny the only Son of God, though you persecute his household, your spirit still remains in that executioner's body of yours, when you consider that the son of Asa too, though he was a sacrilegist like you, reigned thirty-five years among the Jews, of whom you have read that it is written: 'He went in the ways of Asa his father and did not turn aside from them, so as to do what was right in the sight of the Lord; but they did not keep away from the high places, and they sacrificed on the high places and burned incense.' See, here too the king is described as having slept in peace. Since, then, he practised idolatry for thirty-five years, do not take it to your glory and say: 'This is why I am not wounded by any blow, this is why I am not already wiped out but still live, possessing the realm of the Roman empire: because I believe rightly, because the faith of Arius is correct, because I did well to remove bishops and have put in their place such men as Arius would have wished.' Do not, I say, glory in this, and be proud though you do these things, when you see that this king held the kingdom thirty-five years and was taken away in peace. If, then, the crime of idolatry could go unpunished for them because they were taken away so, it will be able to for you too, Constantius. Turn yourself therefore to the Lord, lest you be found such as Ahab was found, of whom I find it written: 'And Ahab did evil in the sight of the Lord, and did more evil than all who were before him. And it was not enough for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, but he also took as wife Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians. And he went and served Baal and worshipped him, and set up a sanctuary of Baal in the house of his religions, which he built in Samaria; and Ahab made a grove, to provoke, to provoke God and destroy his own soul, and he did more evil than all the kings of Israel who were before him.' Do not let yourself remain any longer among the Arians, but cross over to us Christians, to whom all heresies are as Baal is. You heretics are now to us as those who sacrificed to idols were to the worshippers of God of those times; believe me, by this heresy of yours you are in our times such as Ahab was too.

So do not be pleased with yourself because God has not paid you back at once, when you see that this Ahab and his wife Jezebel, who even killed the prophets of the Lord, who are found to have been engaged in so great a crime that they let no man who confessed himself God's remain in the land of Israel, were spared for a very long time. Do not look at this, that though you do evil you are nevertheless proud in your crimes; but see this, I beg you, that unless you turn, just as the deserts of their works were paid back to them, though late, so they can be presented to you too. Do not say: 'This is why I have long been on the throne, this is why I am powerful: because I hold the good faith, because I act rightly in persecuting those who believe as that faith written at Nicaea holds.' Do not, I say, say these things, but see this, I pray you: that you are proud even after so many killings of yours only to this end, that either, listening to us priests of God, you may turn to God, or else that you may receive the due of your deeds at the time when you will not be able to say that you erred unknowingly. Take note that this is so, warned by the example of Ahab, the killer of the Lord's prophets and the worshipper of all demons. Understand that this man, so wicked, was kept on the throne a long time after such great crimes so that he might at last turn, if he would; to him not only were the deserts of his evil deeds not presented, but he was even helped in his straits, without doubt so that he could gather that he had been avenged not through Baal and the other demons whom the heathen call gods, but through the God of Israel, whose prophet he saw speaking with him and declaring to him how God would bring the enemies of the Israelites to nothing. For the son of Hadad, king [of Syria], had besieged Samaria with thirty-two other kings, boasting that he held the Israelites as so much nothing that he alone, one man, would overcome the whole multitude of the Israelites. God made this foreigner nothing before Israel. For which king did God conquer? Why, for Ahab, the one who had forsaken him, who had made Israel serve Baal and all the demons; and he helped him for this reason, namely that he might believe that he alone is God, whose people Israel was, and no other besides him, who had conquered for him, so that Ahab might see that it was right that he should at last correct his errors. As soon as the enemy began to build siege-works against the city of the Israelites, 'behold,' says holy scripture, 'a prophet came to the king of Israel and said: Thus says the Lord: Have you heard this great noise? Behold, today I will deliver it into your hands, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And the king said: By whom? And the prophet said: By the young men of the princes of the provinces. And the king said: Who will join battle? And the prophet said: You.' And below: 'And the young men of the princes of the provinces went out from the city, and the army that followed them, and each struck down the one he found beside him, and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued.' How can you say, Constantius: 'If I did not serve God well, if I had not believed rightly, I would never have seen the kingdom of the Romans placed in my power, or lived so long on the throne'? When you see that to Ahab, king of Israel, who lived in the manner of the gentiles and turned the people of God away from God, as you too turn them away, it was said by him against whom he was sinning, whose precepts he taught were worth nothing: 'I deliver it into your hands, that you may know that I am God.' So he who rescued him from the son of Hadad, king of Syria, has likewise rescued and is rescuing you from all who wish to destroy you, surely to this end, that you may recognise that he is the God of the patriarchs and martyrs, to this end, that you may gather that victory has not been granted you for the merits of your faith and life, since you are like king Ahab in all things, but that mercy has been shown you against your merits by him whom you have forsaken, just as it was shown to Ahab. For if you say that you conquer your enemies because you believe rightly, Ahab too, the worshipper of idols and slayer of the holy prophets, could have said it. Do you not see, then, that you were kept for this, to correct your errors? As soon as you seized Italy, you tried to overturn its church; you said that God the Father is not true God the Father, denying his only Son, affirming that he is not the true Son. You also asserted that the holy Spirit, the Paraclete, was fashioned out of nothing; you tried to maintain that there was a time when the only Son of God was not; you gave all your strength to the task of removing from the midst the apostolic and evangelical tradition by whatever means you could; you had bishops ordained by the judgement of God removed by your authority, and you thought fit to set heretics in their places who could preach your heresy; you fought with military force against the church in Alexandria; you banished a great many of the bishops into exile, into the mines; you cast them into prison; you even killed a certain number of all the worshippers of God. Though you have done these things, you still say: 'Unless I were doing well and believing soundly, God would never let me reign till now,' as though God had been patient with Ahab and your other fellow-idolaters for this reason, that they held the right way. So because he is patient with your sins out of his untiring goodness, as he was with king Ahab too, you think that you do not sin, but are spared for your merits; you imitate Ahab in this too, that you love those who urge evil on you, and destroy those who tell you what is true for the sake of your salvation. For as those four hundred false prophets told Ahab that he could achieve every success, while Micaiah, the prophet of God, said on the contrary that every evil would befall him, and Ahab loved those false prophets more than the true prophet of the Lord, so you too love your fellow-heretics the Arians, obey their words, and curse all of us priests of the Lord: first of all, because we confess the Son of God to be the true Son of God; secondly, because we do not flatter you, because we assert that you are in danger and say that unless you turn to God you will come to eternal punishment.

And so that you may believe that men of God have always been held in hatred by apostate men, while the enemies of God's religion, that is, the worshippers of the devil, have been loved, hear whom Ahab loved and whom he held in hatred. 'And Jehoshaphat king of Judah said to the king of Israel: Inquire now today of the Lord. And the king of Israel called together all the prophets, about four hundred men, and king Ahab said to them: Shall I go to Ramah of Gilead to battle, or shall I refrain? And they said: Go up.' And further on: 'And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel: Is there not a prophet of the Lord here, and we will inquire of the Lord? And Ahab king of Israel said to king Jehoshaphat: There is one through whom we may inquire of the Lord, but I hate him, because he does not speak good things of me.' Again, after Micaiah, the prophet of the Lord, had told him not to go up, because if he went up he would not return: 'The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: Did I not say to you that this man prophesies to me not good things but rather evil?' To him, wicked and senseless, whom the devil had already possessed, the things said by the servant of God seemed evil, and the things said by the servants of the devil were judged good. It is no wonder, then, if Ahab listened to those whom the devil made him listen to, that is, his own slaves, and if he would not listen to those whom God showed to be his servants, both by their very endurance of sufferings and by the very steadfastness of their assertion. The false prophets were sent away by the king enriched and honoured, but Micaiah, the prophet of the Lord, is shut up in prison, and it is said: 'Let him eat the bread of affliction until I return'; and yet, according to the word of the servant of God, he did not return at all. So you too act, Constantius: you love those who drag you with them to everlasting death, who lead your soul to utter destruction, and on the other hand you see fit to hate those who desire that you become a friend of God. Do not boast that, though you do such things, you still possess this frail life, strong in the glory of a kingdom, since the sacred writings relate that Jeroboam son of Joash too reigned in Israel forty-one years in Samaria, though he had forsaken God and served idols, and did not depart from the wickedness of Ahab king of Israel and the sacrifices of Jeroboam. 'If I had done evil,' you say, 'God would already have removed me from the kingdom'; as though the son of Amaziah, because he did not depart from vain things, was not indeed filled with leprosy, but nevertheless reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. But you are worse than king Uzziah in this, that you have not the elephantiasis that could consume all your limbs, but that which can stain the soul through and through. Grieve for yourself with us and shed tears for yourself; observe how this visible elephantiasis stains the body, how the poison of leprosy consumes the limbs. Understand that in the same way the Arian heresy, your elephantiasis, stains all that is within you; mark that it does to your inner man just what this does which has seized those whom you see covered with elephantiasis. Do not say: 'Unless I acted well, I would never have ruled so long, I would never have been allowed to live till now,' since you see that Manasseh too, son of king Hezekiah, king of Judah, took up the kingdom at sixteen years old and reigned fifty-seven years; when you have heard what is written of him, you will surely find that you are his imitator, and you will not begin to wonder that, though you do evil, you are still spared, seeing that Manasseh, than whom you are no less in cruelty and sacrilege, held the kingdom fifty-seven years while doing such things. 'And Hezekiah slept with his fathers,' says the scripture, 'and was buried in the city of David, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place. Manasseh was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-seven years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Hephzibah. And he did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord cast out before the face of the sons of Israel. And he built the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed, and built a sanctuary of Baal and made groves as Ahab king of Israel did, and worshipped all the host of heaven and served them. And he built a sanctuary in the two courts of the house of the Lord, and made his sons pass into the fire, and practised augury, and made many familiar spirits and diviners, to do what is evil in the eyes of his soul, to provoke the Lord God. And he made the carved images of the groves, which he made in the house of which the Lord said to David and to Solomon his son: In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, [I will] put my name for ever, and I will not again set the foot of Israel to move from the land which I gave, but only if they hear me in all that I commanded them, and according to the law which my servant Moses commanded them. And they did not hear. And because Manasseh despised [the Lord] greatly, and Manasseh led them astray to do what is evil beyond all the nations which the Lord removed from before the face of Israel. And the Lord spoke by the hand of his servants the prophets: [Because of] the images which Manasseh king of Judah made, according to all that the Amorite did who was before him, and he made Judah sin with his idols, therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I bring evils upon Jerusalem and upon Judah; all who hear these things, both their ears shall tingle. And I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring-line of Samaria and the weight of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe out Jerusalem as boxwood is wiped from a doorpost before his face. And I will give them into the hands of his enemies, and they shall be for plunder and burning to all their enemies, because they have been cast out from behind me, and they were behind me and were provoking me, from the day their fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day. And the rest of the words of Manasseh and all that he did, how he made Israel sin, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Judah, and how he shed very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem up to the brim, besides the sin by which he made Judah sin, to do what is evil in the sight of the Lord God? And Manasseh slept with his fathers, and his son Amon reigned in his place, being twenty-two years old.'

What do you say to this, Constantius? I believe you now stop saying: 'If I were not acting well, I would not have been reigning so long,' since you see that this other Manasseh too, doing such things, reigned fifty-seven years; and since we have said that you are another Manasseh, see that you have all that was his. He set up idolatry in the house of God; you yourself have done just as much in the temple and courts of the Lord. He caused idols to be worshipped, he usurped for himself what was called the Lord's, so that thereafter it could be called the idols'; all this you too have done, because you brought the Arian heresy into the church, and you decreed that your blasphemy be accepted as the catholic faith, while you command that the [faith] written at Nicaea, which we know to be apostolic and evangelical, be spat upon. As you now have desired these things to be done, so Manasseh too commanded that all idols be served and God be forsaken. It will not be a wonder, then, if you have claimed for yourself the buildings in which we were accustomed to gather the people of God, and, an idolater, have called yourself catholic, since you see that Manasseh too did what you have now done; so in the end the Lord will spare you too as you keep to the way of Manasseh, as he spared him and as long as he spared him, so that it is written that he slept with his fathers and was buried in Jerusalem and his son took up the kingdom in his place. Do you read that he perished in war or was weighed down by some illness? Not at all. But what do you think? I suppose, with that prudence of yours, you say all those things went unpunished for king Manasseh. You are such as to think this of Manasseh: that because he reigned fifty-seven years, handed the kingdom to his son, and himself died in peace, such great crimes could have gone unpunished for him. Do not have pity on yourself so as to turn to God, do not correct your wicked deeds, and you will find yourself tormented with Manasseh, whom you are seen to surpass in this, that he shed the blood of the righteous only within the bounds of Jerusalem, but you have shed and are shedding it throughout the whole Roman empire. 'But,' you say, 'he burned or consecrated his sons before the images of his gods'; and if you had had [sons], you would without doubt have made them accept the Arian blasphemy. Or do you not know that, as those who burned their sons pleased the devil then, since they had one mind, to forsake the Creator and serve the creature, so now the devil demands nothing of you except that you deny the only-begotten Son of God? This is the sacrifice most acceptable to him, that you believe as Arius believed; in our times this is more to him, that you deny the Son of God, than if you were willing to be burned in fire in honour of all the demons. For he sees that the worship of idols is despised by all, because it was a vain invention; now he desires through you, his servants the heretics, to deceive us, the servants of God. 'How,' you say, 'deceive?' As he has already deceived you, so he wants us to be deceived. Though you are an Arian, you pretend to be a Christian for this purpose, that you may wound the defenceless with the poison of your heresy, so that thereafter they may be not what we are, Christians, but what you are, Arians. This is the fattened offering of your services, which is presented through you to the demons. For who but the devil and his sons can say of the only-begotten Son of God: 'He is a son and is not a true son; he is God and is not true God'? So when you say, 'I am a Christian, but I do not believe that God has a true Son, I do not believe in one power of the Father and the Son,' when you call the Son a creature, made out of nothing, when you say there was [a time] when he was not, you sacrifice to the devil better than Manasseh did then, when he either consecrated his sons through fire to all the demons or burned them.

I grieve for you, emperor, that, though you are of such great folly and though you are doing such great evils, you nevertheless see fit to say: 'If I were not doing well, I would not still be on the throne; God would already have destroyed me.' Do you not see that Manasseh, who is to be compared with you in sacrilege and in cruelty, held the kingdom in Judaea for fifty-seven years, as I have often said? He is certainly the one who made the people forsake God and serve idols; he is certainly the one who set up images in the temple of the Lord and in the house of God, who made the house of God, the sanctuary of his majesty, a sanctuary of idols. So God bears with you too, so he endures you, until he both tests his own household and crowns the worthy and punishes the unworthy along with you, unless you correct yourself, with eternal punishment. For the rest, believe that he could, both then Manasseh and now you, destroy [you] in a single twinkling of the eyes; but he spares, not because he cannot, but because it is fitting both that his worshippers be crowned, remaining unmoved against your cruelty, and that he condemn you, the enemies of his clemency, to everlasting punishment, if you resolve to persist such as you are. That you say, 'If I were not acting well, I would never still be ruling,' is the work of those who not only do not want you to be corrected in your error, but even drive you on to perish. No wonder; for it is written that both you and they would be such: 'The sinner is praised in the desires of his soul, and he who does wicked things will be blessed. The sinner has provoked the Lord; according to the greatness of his wrath he will not seek [him]; God is not before his sight; his ways are defiled at all times; your judgements are taken away from his face.' So when you say, 'We do well to remove those bishops who confess that they hold the faith written at Nicaea, and to appoint those who confess as Arius confessed,' and they say, 'Rightly indeed,' you are that sinner who is unjustly praised for the desires of your soul; and you are the wicked one who, though you have been forsaken by God for your blasphemies, nevertheless, with your flatterers, are not rebuked for whatever wrong you do, but rather it is said that you act well. When you say, 'I did well to send soldiers to Alexandria to remove Athanasius,' and they say, 'Most rightly,' to whom will you be compared, if not to the one who is marked out by the Holy Spirit through the psalmist, in that, though he does wicked things, though he is most wicked and accursed, he nevertheless longs to be praised? You say, 'Unless I were acting well, God would not still have spared me'; and I find it said to God: 'Therefore you correct little by little those who have strayed, and, admonishing, you speak to those who sin, so that, having abandoned wickedness, they may believe in you, Lord. For hating those ancient inhabitants of your land, because they did works hateful to you through sorceries and unrighteous rites, and [being] merciless slayers of their children, you willed to destroy [them] by the hands of our fathers, so that the land which is dearest to you of all might receive a worthy settlement of the children of God. Yet even these, as men, you spared, and you sent wasps as forerunners of your army, to destroy them little by little. Were you unable to subject the ungodly to the righteous in battle, or to destroy [them] at once by most savage beasts or by a harsh word? But judging little by little you gave room for repentance, not unaware that their nation was wicked and their malice inborn, and that their way of thinking could never be changed; for they were a seed accursed from the beginning; nor, fearing anyone, did you grant pardon for their sins. For who will say to you, "What have you done?" or who will stand against your judgement?'

In the same way you too are spared, Constantius, so that you may do penance or perish after the example of those who, though they were known by God not to be going to do penance, not to be going to turn themselves to God, because [their] seed was evil from the beginning, he nevertheless spared, and did not punish them as soon as they sinned. So do not say, 'If I were not acting well, God would certainly never have spared me,' when you see that a long space for repentance was granted to your partners in crime, so that they might at last see the causes of their evil deeds and make satisfaction to God for the offence. You too, then, if you do not turn to God, will be one of that accursed race of which it is said to God: 'not unaware that their nation was wicked and their malice inborn, and that their way of thinking could never be changed; for they were a seed accursed from the beginning.' How glorious, then, will you see yourself to be, when you begin to be with such people, when you see yourself judged among such, when, found among such, you are sent into the unquenchable flames? You will certainly be first of all and greatest there too in those punishments; for no one could be found your equal in wickedness except the devil alone, so that anyone could be seen as better than you in those punishments. You dare to say: 'If I did not live well, if my works were not right, if my faith, that is the Arian, had not been catholic, if I had not acted rightly in removing those bishops who preach the faith set down by the three hundred and more at Nicaea, I would never reign long, I would never shine so brightly in the kingdom that, though for a short time, I alone ruled within the Roman frontier.' If it is as you say, why does Job, the most righteous worshipper of God, say to those who were attacking his righteousness with false charges: 'Hear me, since the pains of my wound compel me to speak: why do the ungodly live, and their houses are not scattered, and fear is far from them? Their cow has never miscarried, it has always carried its womb [to term]; and they themselves remain like sheep for ever, and their sons, taking up the instrument, play with delight, so that they spend their life in good things, though the Lord says: "Depart from me, you wicked; I do not wish to know their ways, since the lamp of the ungodly will be put out and they will grieve with groaning in their life. They will be like chaff which is carried off by the wind, or like dust which is whirled by the storm; and let their eyes see death." Since I know that the Lord has said these things about them, know that none of you can restrain me so that I keep silent.' Why does the most glorious Job say these things? Only because he knew that very many indeed act wickedly and yet their deserts are not repaid at once, but they are kept for this, that they either correct themselves or at least after death feel the punishments of their offences, feel what it meant not to have sought God, not to have served him while there was opportunity, and to win his favour by believing in him alone and serving him. Now, I believe, convinced by the testimony of so great a man, you will cease to say that you acted justly in removing the priests of the Lord and ordaining men of the Arian faith and ordering the faith of the Arian doctrine to be preached, in proscribing and deporting and applying tortures to and killing those who believe in the only-begotten Son of God; you will cease, I say, to say that you live and flourish thus in the kingdom because you have done and are doing those things, when you hear the righteous man Job, whom God said had served him without complaint, whom he declared his true worshipper, saying that, though very many act ungodly, they nevertheless live most pleasantly in this life. Further, deign to receive what he says below about you ungodly ones, and learn how, though you act wickedly, you are spared for the time being, and present yourself to God through penance: 'I did not know that such darkness would come before my face. Why then, Lord, could I not lie hidden for one hour? But the ungodly pass over into others' borders, and they have seized flocks of sheep with their shepherds, and they have afflicted the cattle of orphans and taken the widow's ox in pledge. They have reaped a field not their own before its time, and they have compelled men to work in their vineyards for nothing. And they have stripped many and taken bread from the hungry, and they have laid siege in many narrow places, and they have not understood the way of righteousness. Let their portion be cursed on the earth. For what hope is there for ungodly men, or what access can they have to the Lord? But even if they have grown strong, they will come to want, and those of them who remain will die an evil death, and no one will pity their widows; and if they have gathered gold or silver like mud, the righteous will possess all these things.' So do not now see fit to flatter yourself unjustly, emperor, since you are such as we have asserted, and to think that you, a murderer and sacrilegist, live so very long in this life because your works are acceptable to God. Your works are such as were the works of those against whom the Holy Spirit inveighs through the mouth of Isaiah, saying: 'Thus says the Lord who freed you, the Holy One of Israel: I am God, I have shown you the way in which you should walk; and if you had heard my commandments, your peace would have become like a river and your righteousness like the waves of the sea, and your seed would have become like the sand of the sea, and the offspring of your womb.'

'But,' you say, 'these things were said to the Jews': yes, to those whom you have made yourself an imitator of. And now, as has often been said, change your wicked ways, believe as the holy Church believes, and he will be gracious to you in all things. For he himself says: 'Return to me with your whole heart, and with fasting and weeping and mourning, and rend your hearts and not your garments.' Return to God with your whole heart; accept these healing remedies, so that you may come to see and understand your crime; open the eyes of your heart; groan with your whole heart, recognising that you have sinned so gravely. Then he will have mercy on you who says: 'When you have turned and groaned, then you will be saved and will know where you have been.' Remember that the prophet consecrated to God said: 'I do not desire the death of the dying, says the Lord, so much as that he should return and live.' Do not now hold the view that, although your works are evil, you are acting well because you have not at once received the punishment for your deeds; but look at what is written, that the Lord is patient, so that you may repent. 'Do not say: I have sinned, and what grievous thing has happened to me? For the Most High is a patient repayer.' Hear also the blessed Paul inviting you to God and disclosing to you how [God] may be appeased toward you: that he is patient, and the deserts of your works are not paid out on the spot, because he wishes you at last to rise up out of evils through repentance, through true satisfaction. 'Do you despise the forbearance of his goodness and his patience, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance? But according to your hardness and impenitent heart you are storing up for yourself wrath on the day of wrath and of the revelation of the just judgement of God, who will render to each according to his work.' Return, Constantius, to God; take up the arms of repentance against the robbery of your inner enemy; flee the ruinous praise of flatterers, who have not deigned to tell you what they have [in their hearts]; remember that the Lord said through the mouth of Isaiah: 'Those who call you happy lead you into error and confuse the path of your feet.' Believe in the only Son of God; receive pardon for your crimes; repeat the words of the psalmist: 'For who will confess to you among the dead?' and again: 'Will dust make confession to you?' Return to God; groan for your crimes; hear the voice of the Lord speaking through Jeremiah: 'Shall he who falls not rise again, or he who turns away not turn back?' You fell on the day when you denied the Son of God; you will rise again in the hour when you confess [him]. Since a wound from the enemy has settled in you, hand yourself over to medicine to be cured; apply the remedy to yourself. You wounded yourself by saying, 'He is not the true Son of God'; you will heal yourself again if you say, as we say and believe, that he is the true Son of God. 'Return,' says Joel, 'to the Lord your God, for he is merciful and kind and patient and of great compassion, and one who turns aside his sentence against the evil imposed.' If you think fit to reject this pardon promised to you for your killings, you will long to obtain it there, where you will receive nothing but the torments of punishment.
